The share price of Intel dropped almost 30% on Friday , shaving over $11 billion from the US government's stake in the company, though the transaction remains profitable overall. Last August, the Trump administration took a 9.9% equity stake in the chipmaker at a price of $20.47 per share, according to a company press release at the time. That initial stake of 433.3 million primary shares was worth about $8.9 billion. The value shot up dramatically earlier this year, with Intel ( INTC ) closing on Thursday at $92.07 per share, implying a value to the US government of $39.9 billion. But the stock took a beating on Friday after the company reported earnings on Thursday night . The stock closed Friday down about 29% at $65.76 per share, suggesting a new paper value for the government's stake of $28.5 billion. The rapid price change underscores how government investments can take investors on a wild ride and presents a new challenge to a centerpiece of Trump's government portfolio, which now spans 40 companies, according to a CATO Institute tracker. Investors punished Intel after its Q4 revenue outlook fell short of Wall Street expectations and the company reported a worse-than-anticipated drop in PC revenue. Intel is projecting fourth quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, well below the $17 billion analysts expected. The company is projecting earnings per share of $0.25 versus forecasts of $0.43. That change in outlook led to losses that, at some points on Friday morning, put Intel on pace for its worst losses since 1974 , as the company as a whole erased nearly $150 billion in market value. The government's investment in Intel — which Trump has promised will yield outsized returns for taxpayers — is a running theme from the White House. In September, an image on Truth Social depicted the president as a stock trader in the Oval Office, with Intel's price displayed on a screen at $95 per share. Trump has previously exaggerated the gains, suggesting at one point, "I've made Hundreds of Billions of Dollars on Stocks, and many other type Holdings, for the U.S.A., not myself." Even so, the investment in Intel remains very profitable and still ended the day on Friday more than three times what the US paid for it. Ben Werschkul is a Washington correspondent for Yahoo Finance.

extraction.body: Apple today took the unusual step of confirming when its next iOS developer beta is expected to arrive, as part of an announcement detailing the upcoming launch of Apple Intelligence in China. Here are the details. In mid-July, Reuters reported that, following a lengthy back-and-forth with Chinese regulators and multiple delays, Apple Intelligence had finally cleared a major regulatory hurdle ahead of its long-awaited launch in the country. Then, a couple of weeks ago, Bloomberg reported that Apple was planning to launch Apple Intelligence in China in December as part of iOS 27.3, although without Siri AI and other newer features. The following day, China’s state-backed media outlet The Paper reported that Tim Cook had confirmed regulatory approval for the platform, with a test version expected before the end of October. Then, just last Monday, Apple released iOS 27.2 and its counterparts, expanding Siri AI support to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. On the same day, the company announced that four more languages, including Traditional Chinese, would be supported by the end of the year. However, while that announcement confirmed additional language support for Siri AI, it offered no updates on the rollout of Apple Intelligence in China, where Siri AI itself will remain unavailable for the time being. While Apple typically releases the first beta of its next software update shortly after the previous version becomes available, iOS 27.3 has yet to materialize. Now, as spotted by MacRumors , a press release published on Apple’s Chinese Newsroom website confirms that testing of Apple Intelligence in China will begin on November 4, as part of the next iOS developer beta. Importantly, Apple has only confirmed November 4 as the start of Apple Intelligence testing in China, not necessarily the release date of iOS 27.3 beta 1 itself. In the press release , Apple confirms that users in China will get an improved Siri experience, including Type to Siri and the ability to access Alibaba’s Qwen for certain requests, but not Siri AI itself. The Qwen integration will also extend to Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence. According to Apple, users will be able to ask questions about photos and documents, including PDFs and presentations, as well as generate original content from scratch through Writing Tools. Users will be able to access Qwen by signing into their accounts or using Sign in with Apple. Other features included in the initial rollout are Live Translation in Messages, FaceTime, and Phone, Writing Tools, Genmoji, Clean Up in Photos, natural-language photo searches, priority notifications, notification summaries, and Smart Reply, among others. Apple also noted that the initial rollout will be exclusive to the iPhone, with support for other platforms coming only after the necessary regulatory approvals have been obtained. The features will be available on the iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max, iPhone 16 and later, iPhone Air, and iPhone Duo, with both Siri and the device language required to be set to either English or Simplified Chinese. The company also confirmed that the features will become publicly available in December, with the official release of iOS 27.3. To check out Apple’s press release, follow this link . extraction.body: Apple is preparing to bring Apple Intelligence to mainland China in December, potentially ending a delay that has kept the company’s AI features out of one of its most important markets for more than two years. According to Bloomberg , Apple is planning to launch its first Apple Intelligence features in the country as part of iOS 27.3. The rollout would mark a major step for Apple in China, where regulatory requirements have prevented the company from offering the same AI experience already available across many other markets. The initial launch is expected to be deliberately limited. Apple reportedly plans to bring over several of the original Apple Intelligence capabilities first introduced in 2024, including Writing Tools, notification summaries, Genmoji and the Clean Up feature in Photos. However, the newer Siri AI experience introduced with iOS 27 is not expected to be included. Apple’s own image-generation tools are also expected to remain unavailable, while some text-generation capabilities could be restricted in certain apps. That means customers in China may receive a noticeably different version of Apple Intelligence from the experience available elsewhere. The rollout has required Apple to take a different technical approach to comply with Chinese regulations. Bloomberg reports that Apple has worked with Alibaba on safeguards for its AI system, including a filtering mechanism designed around local requirements, while Baidu is involved in areas including search and Siri. A separate South China Morning Post report says updated network access permits from China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology now list Apple Intelligence alongside Alibaba’s Qwen and Tongyi Wanxiang models for devices including the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro and several earlier iPhones. Apple has been trying to bring Apple Intelligence to China since the platform was first introduced in 2024. Earlier launch targets reportedly slipped repeatedly as the company worked through regulatory approval, local model requirements and the restrictions placed on foreign-developed generative AI services. The absence of Apple Intelligence has become increasingly important for Apple as Chinese smartphone makers continue to push AI deeper into their devices. Rivals including Huawei, Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo already offer extensive generative AI features, leaving Apple without one of the headline capabilities it promotes elsewhere around the world. Bringing Writing Tools, notification summaries and other everyday Apple Intelligence features to Chinese iPhone users would close part of the gap, while giving Apple a foundation it could expand if further approvals are secured. coreStoryFacts.text: Importantly, Apple has only confirmed November 4 as the start of Apple Intelligence testing in China, not necessarily the release date of iOS 27.3 beta 1 itself.

In the press release , Apple confirms that users in China will get an improved Siri experience, including Type to Siri and the ability to access Alibaba’s Qwen for certain requests, but not Siri AI itself.
Then, just last Monday, Apple released iOS 27.2 and its counterparts, expanding Siri AI support to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.
On the same day, the company announced that four more languages, including Traditional Chinese, would be supported by the end of the year.

In mid-July, Reuters reported that, following a lengthy back-and-forth with Chinese regulators and multiple delays, Apple Intelligence had finally cleared a major regulatory hurdle ahead of its long-awaited launch in the country.
The Qwen integration will also extend to Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence.
According to Apple, users will be able to ask questions about photos and documents, including PDFs and presentations, as well as generate original content from scratch through Writing Tools.
Apple also noted that the initial rollout will be exclusive to the iPhone, with support for other platforms coming only after the necessary regulatory approvals have been obtained.

Instead, Apple is launching several of its earlier Apple Intelligence features like notification summaries, real-time translation, rewriting and proofreading tools, visual intelligence, and removing objects from photos.

It initially thought an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing unauthorised withdrawals, but later said the attack was wider. The US Secret Service said it was "working around the clock" "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover" stolen funds. The firm said $3bn of its stolen digital assets had been secured - but many were still in the hands of unidentified hackers. It initially thought an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing unauthorised withdrawals, but later said the attack was wider. Several analytics firms have linked the hack, which eclipses a $1.5bn (£1.12bn) heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit. The US Secret Service said it was "working around the clock" "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover" stolen funds. America's lead federal agency for investigating financial crimes added that it would "identify the cyber criminals responsible and bring them to justice", while Binance also said it was working with the FBI. While Binance said its US-facing exchange was unaffected, the US would still have jurisdiction to investigate the hack and help track down stolen funds - an effort which generally involves a global law enforcement effort. The hack also involved some US-linked assets, such as stablecoins Tether and Circle – cryptocurrencies pegged to the dollar. Who could be behind the Binance hack and what we know so far Binance's co-CEO Richard Teng said: "This was not carried out by one person. Our initial investigation suggested that the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop, however our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach." Teng also describes how the hackers used "a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and traces as they went, making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate". Initially, the company had indicated the breach "may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop" but later statements have pointed to a broader breach. In a later update, the firm said it had "set aside" more than $6.34B in company funds to cover the stolen assets and was "actively buying" a range of crypto tokens. The firm said $3bn of its stolen digital assets had been secured - but many were still in the hands of unidentified hackers. It initially thought an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing unauthorised withdrawals, but later said the attack was wider. Several analytics firms have linked the hack, which eclipses a $1.5bn (£1.12bn) heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit. The US Secret Service said it was "working around the clock" "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover" stolen funds. America's lead federal agency for investigating financial crimes added that it would "identify the cyber criminals responsible and bring them to justice", while Binance also said it was working with the FBI. While Binance said its US-facing exchange was unaffected, the US would still have jurisdiction to investigate the hack and help track down stolen funds - an effort which generally involves a global law enforcement effort. Binance told its users "your money is safe, and we're covering every loss". It had initially suspended all deposits and withdrawals - but then said in an update that "deposits remain unaffected". Binance's co-CEO Richard Teng said: "This was not carried out by one person. Our initial investigation suggested that the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop, however our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach." Teng also describes how the hackers used "a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and traces as they went, making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate". Initially, the company had indicated the breach "may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop" but later statements have pointed to a broader breach. In a later update, the firm said it had "set aside" more than $6.34B in company funds to cover the stolen assets and was "actively buying" a range of crypto tokens. The names refer to clusters of cyber criminals accused of working directly for the regime. It makes North Korea likely to be the only nation that uses hacking as a way to raise public funds.

Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals after reporting a security breach involving approximately $6.3 billion in stolen digital assets, triggering losses across cryptocurrency markets and shares of companies exposed to the sector. Bitcoin fell sharply following the announcement, while Ether, Binance's BNB token and several cryptocurrency-related stocks also recorded significant declines. Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, confirmed that an attacker had exploited a security vulnerability to carry out unauthorised withdrawals. The company estimated the total financial impact at $6.3 billion, making the incident substantially larger than previous cryptocurrency exchange hacks. According to Binance, the breach originated from a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer. The attacker used the compromised device to execute unauthorised withdrawals from the exchange. Binance said its investigation had found no evidence that private keys associated with cryptocurrency wallets had been exposed. The distinction is significant because private keys provide direct control over digital assets held in cryptocurrency wallets. The company has temporarily halted withdrawals while it conducts security checks and works to prevent further unauthorised transactions. Binance indicated that it expects the suspension to last no longer than 48 hours, although the resumption of withdrawals remains dependent on the completion of its security procedures. Binance said it had coordinated with industry partners to freeze approximately $3 billion of the assets affected by the attack. The exchange also committed to reimbursing all losses from its own financial resources. Circle, the company behind the USDC stablecoin, confirmed that it had frozen more than 800 million USDC linked to the breach. Tether separately reported freezing more than 1.567 billion USDT associated with the attack. The measures were intended to prevent the movement of stolen funds and limit the financial consequences of the incident. Binance co-founder and former Chief Executive Changpeng Zhao also commented on the situation. "It does look like a hack on Binance," Zhao said in a social media post. The company's commitment to cover losses and restore withdrawals will remain an important factor in determining how quickly confidence returns among its users. The absence of a reported reduction in BNB holdings contrasted with the substantial losses involving Bitcoin, stablecoins and other cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency by market capitalisation, fell 2.5% to $78,106.60. During the initial market reaction, the token dropped as low as $76,518 before recovering part of its losses. The selloff reflected concerns about exchange security, the potential impact on market liquidity and uncertainty surrounding the recovery of stolen assets. The temporary suspension of withdrawals also added to investor caution as Binance worked to complete its security review. The market reaction extended beyond cryptocurrencies to publicly traded companies with significant exposure to digital assets. The latest security incident introduced additional uncertainty for businesses whose performance is closely linked to the adoption and trading of digital assets. The immediate focus for cryptocurrency markets will be Binance's progress in completing its security checks and restoring withdrawal services. The exchange has indicated that withdrawals should resume within 48 hours and that it intends to absorb the financial losses associated with the incident.

“Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information,” the statement added. “Users should remain cautious of scams and should not trust unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information.”
Zhao, who no longer runs the company but is its largest shareholder, said that he expects users’ funds to be “fully covered” but did not provide an explanation for the claim.

sources.title: It Took Hackers Just 20 Minutes to Steal $6.3 Billion in Crypto from a Single Platform - Futurism
passages: Crypto exchange Binance suspended withdrawals after elite hackers stole a staggering $6.3 billion in digital assets, marking what may be the biggest crypto heist of all time.

Researchers at the crypto research firm TRM Labs told the New York Times that they have “high confidence” in its assessment that the theft was the work of “North Korea’s elite hacking unit.” It reportedly took just 20 minutes to drain Binance of billions of dollars in crypto.
Previously, crypto’s biggest heist was last February’s attack on Binance rival Bybit, according to NYT .
That attack was also carried out by North Korean hackers, who made away with $1.5 billion.
Crypto has always been risky — and even riskier now that cybercriminals have access to advanced AI tools that are supercharging hacking efforts across the digital world.
I’m a senior staff writer at Futurism, investigating how the rise of artificial intelligence is impacting the media, internet, and information ecosystems.

Binance founder Changpeng “CZ” Zhao said on X that “user funds are safe,” but the incident “does look like a hack.” Zhao, a major player in the crypto world, pleaded guilty to money laundering and was sentenced to four months in prison in 2024 but was pardoned last year by president Donald Trump after Binance provided support to World Liberty Financial, the Trump family’s much-scrutinized crypto venture. (Zhao is no longer Binance’s CEO, but is still a shareholder.)

coreStoryFacts.text: Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals after reporting a security breach involving approximately $6.3 billion in stolen digital assets, triggering losses across cryptocurrency markets and shares of companies exposed to the sector.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Bitcoin fell sharply following the announcement, while Ether, Binance's BNB token and several cryptocurrency-related stocks also recorded significant declines.
The attacker also withdrew 17,985 Bitcoin, valued at approximately $1.45 billion at the time.
Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency by market capitalisation, fell 2.5% to $78,106.60.
Binance said it had coordinated with industry partners to freeze approximately $3 billion of the assets affected by the attack.
The absence of a reported reduction in BNB holdings contrasted with the substantial losses involving Bitcoin, stablecoins and other cryptocurrencies.
The immediate focus for cryptocurrency markets will be Binance's progress in completing its security checks and restoring withdrawal services.
Binance indicated that it expects the suspension to last no longer than 48 hours, although the resumption of withdrawals remains dependent on the completion of its security procedures.
"It does look like a hack on Binance," Zhao said in a social media post.
Binance said its investigation had found no evidence that private keys associated with cryptocurrency wallets had been exposed.
Binance has confirmed to TechCrunch that it is dealing with a security incident as users reported that funds were being drained from the crypto exchange’s wallets.
By some estimates, Binance may have lost upward of $5.7 billion in crypto , though the numbers have not been confirmed and it’s possible that the theft is ongoing.
Financial tech giant Circle froze about $800 million in Tether as it passed through its networks, while crypto giant Tether froze about $1.56 billion related to Binance’s hack.
“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” Binance said in a statement.

“Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information,” the statement added. “Users should remain cautious of scams and should not trust unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information.”
Zhao, who no longer runs the company but is its largest shareholder, said that he expects users’ funds to be “fully covered” but did not provide an explanation for the claim.

Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Bitcoin fell sharply following the announcement, while Ether, Binance's BNB token and several cryptocurrency-related stocks also recorded significant declines.
The attacker also withdrew 17,985 Bitcoin, valued at approximately $1.45 billion at the time.
Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency by market capitalisation, fell 2.5% to $78,106.60.
Binance said it had coordinated with industry partners to freeze approximately $3 billion of the assets affected by the attack.
The absence of a reported reduction in BNB holdings contrasted with the substantial losses involving Bitcoin, stablecoins and other cryptocurrencies.
The immediate focus for cryptocurrency markets will be Binance's progress in completing its security checks and restoring withdrawal services.
Binance indicated that it expects the suspension to last no longer than 48 hours, although the resumption of withdrawals remains dependent on the completion of its security procedures.
"It does look like a hack on Binance," Zhao said in a social media post.
Binance said its investigation had found no evidence that private keys associated with cryptocurrency wallets had been exposed.
Binance has confirmed to TechCrunch that it is dealing with a security incident as users reported that funds were being drained from the crypto exchange’s wallets.
By some estimates, Binance may have lost upward of $5.7 billion in crypto , though the numbers have not been confirmed and it’s possible that the theft is ongoing.
Financial tech giant Circle froze about $800 million in Tether as it passed through its networks, while crypto giant Tether froze about $1.56 billion related to Binance’s hack.
“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” Binance said in a statement.

“Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information,” the statement added. “Users should remain cautious of scams and should not trust unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information.”
Zhao, who no longer runs the company but is its largest shareholder, said that he expects users’ funds to be “fully covered” but did not provide an explanation for the claim.

Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals after reporting a security breach involving approximately $6.3 billion in stolen digital assets, triggering losses across cryptocurrency markets and shares of companies exposed to the sector. The incident, disclosed on Thursday evening, represents the largest reported cryptocurrency theft on record, according to the exchange. Binance said it had worked with industry partners to freeze approximately $3 billion in affected assets and would cover all losses using its own funds. The exchange expects withdrawals to resume within 48 hours, subject to the completion of additional security checks. Bitcoin fell sharply following the announcement, while Ether, Binance's BNB token and several cryptocurrency-related stocks also recorded significant declines. Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, confirmed that an attacker had exploited a security vulnerability to carry out unauthorised withdrawals. The company estimated the total financial impact at $6.3 billion, making the incident substantially larger than previous cryptocurrency exchange hacks. According to Binance, the breach originated from a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer. The attacker used the compromised device to execute unauthorised withdrawals from the exchange. Binance said its investigation had found no evidence that private keys associated with cryptocurrency wallets had been exposed. The distinction is significant because private keys provide direct control over digital assets held in cryptocurrency wallets. The company has temporarily halted withdrawals while it conducts security checks and works to prevent further unauthorised transactions. Binance indicated that it expects the suspension to last no longer than 48 hours, although the resumption of withdrawals remains dependent on the completion of its security procedures. Binance said it had coordinated with industry partners to freeze approximately $3 billion of the assets affected by the attack. The exchange also committed to reimbursing all losses from its own financial resources. Circle, the company behind the USDC stablecoin, confirmed that it had frozen more than 800 million USDC linked to the breach. Tether separately reported freezing more than 1.567 billion USDT associated with the attack. The measures were intended to prevent the movement of stolen funds and limit the financial consequences of the incident. Binance co-founder and former Chief Executive Changpeng Zhao also commented on the situation. "It does look like a hack on Binance," Zhao said in a social media post. The company's commitment to cover losses and restore withdrawals will remain an important factor in determining how quickly confidence returns among its users. According to its data, the stolen assets included approximately $1.66 billion in Tether's USDT stablecoin. The attacker also withdrew 17,985 Bitcoin, valued at approximately $1.45 billion at the time. A further $767 million in USDC was transferred from the exchange. The figures illustrate the scale and diversity of the digital assets involved in the incident. Glassnode also reported that Binance's holdings of its native BNB token were "left untouched." The absence of a reported reduction in BNB holdings contrasted with the substantial losses involving Bitcoin, stablecoins and other cryptocurrencies. Cryptocurrency prices declined following the disclosure of the security breach, extending losses recorded earlier in the week. Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency by market capitalisation, fell 2.5% to $78,106.60. During the initial market reaction, the token dropped as low as $76,518 before recovering part of its losses. The selloff reflected concerns about exchange security, the potential impact on market liquidity and uncertainty surrounding the recovery of stolen assets. The temporary suspension of withdrawals also added to investor caution as Binance worked to complete its security review. The market reaction extended beyond cryptocurrencies to publicly traded companies with significant exposure to digital assets. The latest security incident introduced additional uncertainty for businesses whose performance is closely linked to the adoption and trading of digital assets. The immediate focus for cryptocurrency markets will be Binance's progress in completing its security checks and restoring withdrawal services. The exchange has indicated that withdrawals should resume within 48 hours and that it intends to absorb the financial losses associated with the incident.

sources.title: It Took Hackers Just 20 Minutes to Steal $6.3 Billion in Crypto from a Single Platform - Futurism
passages: Crypto exchange Binance suspended withdrawals after elite hackers stole a staggering $6.3 billion in digital assets, marking what may be the biggest crypto heist of all time.

Researchers at the crypto research firm TRM Labs told the New York Times that they have “high confidence” in its assessment that the theft was the work of “North Korea’s elite hacking unit.” It reportedly took just 20 minutes to drain Binance of billions of dollars in crypto.
Previously, crypto’s biggest heist was last February’s attack on Binance rival Bybit, according to NYT .
That attack was also carried out by North Korean hackers, who made away with $1.5 billion.
Crypto has always been risky — and even riskier now that cybercriminals have access to advanced AI tools that are supercharging hacking efforts across the digital world.
I’m a senior staff writer at Futurism, investigating how the rise of artificial intelligence is impacting the media, internet, and information ecosystems.

Binance founder Changpeng “CZ” Zhao said on X that “user funds are safe,” but the incident “does look like a hack.” Zhao, a major player in the crypto world, pleaded guilty to money laundering and was sentenced to four months in prison in 2024 but was pardoned last year by president Donald Trump after Binance provided support to World Liberty Financial, the Trump family’s much-scrutinized crypto venture. (Zhao is no longer Binance’s CEO, but is still a shareholder.)

extraction.body: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record. The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets had been frozen but that many remained in the hands of the hackers, adding that it will "cover all losses". The company said while initial checks suggested an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, "our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach". Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor. Cyber-security firm Check Point said the unit is also known in the industry as Lazarus Group, which has been blamed for the 2025 hack. Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record". AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack. The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen. The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added. Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide. The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under its custody. The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world. Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack. For the last few years North Korea-linked operatives have focussed on attacking cryptocurrency companies for large thefts of digital tokens. Western security agencies have previously said stolen funds are used to finance North Korea's nuclear weapons and missile development programs. The regime has denied any involvement in hacks in the past. Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' Head of Research, urged every exchange to remain vigilant as the platforms are attractive targets for hackers due to the sheer value of assets. Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice." The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue. Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop. "That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions," he said in a statement. In an update, the company said in a statement on X that another investigation found there had been other breach points: "We are still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them." Check Point's Dave said this attack also resembled a hack on crypto exchange platform Bitget in September in which $388m (£289m) was lost: "This implies that attackers no longer need the vault keys. They target the systems and people with authority to use them." In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets. "Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said. Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack. World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it has worked with its partners to freeze stolen funds. Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation. Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue. Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply. If the accusations are true, the record-making heist shows how powerful suspected North Korean hackers have become. The cyber-attack, which the company describes as complex, is believed to be the largest ever of its kind. Cyber correspondent Joe Tidy explains more about what is suspected to be the biggest hack in history. The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under its custody.
The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world.
Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack.
For the last few years North Korea-linked operatives have focussed on attacking cryptocurrency companies for large thefts of digital tokens.
Western security agencies have previously said stolen funds are used to finance North Korea's nuclear weapons and missile development programs.
The regime has denied any involvement in hacks in the past.
Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' Head of Research, urged every exchange to remain vigilant as the platforms are attractive targets for hackers due to the sheer value of assets.

Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."

The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue.
Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop.
"That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions," he said in a statement.

In an update, the company said in a statement on X that another investigation found there had been other breach points: "We are still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them."

Check Point's Dave said this attack also resembled a hack on crypto exchange platform Bitget in September in which $388m (£289m) was lost: "This implies that attackers no longer need the vault keys. They target the systems and people with authority to use them."
In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets.
"Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said.
Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.
World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it has worked with its partners to freeze stolen funds.
Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation.
Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue.
Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply.
If the accusations are true, the record-making heist shows how powerful suspected North Korean hackers have become.
The cyber-attack, which the company describes as complex, is believed to be the largest ever of its kind.

sources.title: Binance hack explained: Bitcoin slumps to $76,400 after the $6.3 billion heist. Are user funds safe? - Kitco
passages: (Kitco Commentary) - The largest crypto theft in history hit while Bitcoin had already broken support, and the timing is right before the midterms.
Here’s how I am positioning before the election.
According to initial reports, about $6.3 billion was drained from the exchange’s hot wallets in minutes, and Bitcoin dropped to a six-week low.
That included 18,270 Bitcoin worth about $1.47 billion, more than 200,000 ETH, and billions in stablecoins.
Binance’s SAFU fund (Secure Asset Fund for Users) was set up in 2018 with $1 billion, and this hack is more than six times that size.
Binance says it will cover the rest with company funds.
Alphabet closed down more than 12% Thursday, the Nasdaq fell 1.4%, and Amazon and Intel both dropped hard after hours.
Ethereum fell to a two-month low around $2,178, and over $1.5 billion in leveraged positions got liquidated, most of them longs.
A few years ago, a $6 billion hack on the biggest exchange in the world could have taken the whole market down with it.
This time Bitcoin dropped about 4% and stabilized.
Binance says about $3 billion has been frozen on-chain, including more than $2.3 billion by Tether and Circle.
That stopped a big chunk of the stolen money from being dumped on the market.
The hack worsened the drop, but Bitcoin was already weak before the news broke.
In yesterday’s article, I pointed out that old support had turned into resistance and that the momentum was pointing down.
I waited until after the FOMC meeting and big tech earnings to write it so I could see how momentum played out, and that turned out to be a wise decision.
Cassius Cuvée is a full-time trader, financial commentator, and trading educator based in the Bay Area of California.
He has traded full-time since 2020 and follows the markets seven days a week, with a focus on Bitcoin and cryptocurrency alongside stocks, precious metals, oil, and bonds.
His specialty is Bitcoin and cryptocurrencies, especially how Bitcoin moves in relation to the NASDAQ and major tech equities.
He studies the markets through a macro lens and the cycles that drive them, but he trades the short term.
He teaches scalping, day trading, and swing trading, and uses that cross-market view to explain price action and the setups he is watching.
Cassius is also a recording artist and a self-described reality rapper, using his words to precisely explain what is happening in his environment, including how the financial markets work.
That same precise approach carries into everything he teaches.
He also runs a YouTube channel with more than 64,000 subscribers and is the creator of Swell Point, a proprietary indicator.
His website, cassiuscuvee.com, produces educational content built to help everyday traders understand what is really moving the markets.
Co-CEO Richard Teng posted on X: “Bottom line - your money is safe, and we’re covering every loss.”
If you believe in Bitcoin for the long term, I still think it’s a good idea to dollar cost average, like I mentioned in my article last Friday.
A dip caused by an exchange getting hacked doesn’t change anything about Bitcoin itself.
Binance says the breach may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which gave the attacker access to a service container where they submitted unauthorized withdrawals.
On Friday, the exchange said it found “additional points of breach,” so the full picture is still coming together.
Here’s the part that should bother every crypto investor: The Bitcoin network wasn’t hacked.
As I write this, Bitcoin is back above $77,000.
Second, Binance’s promise to cover every loss kept a lot of people from panic selling.
The bottom line is that users are covered only as long as Binance keeps that promise.
Until withdrawals reopen, nobody can move their money off the exchange.

coreStoryFacts.text: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record.
The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.
Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record".
Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.

Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."
Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue.
AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop.
Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack.
Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation.
In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets.
US Secret Service says it is helping to track funds stolen from crypto firm Binance in $6.3bn hack
Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, says it has "begun recovering" some funds and believes there was more than one hacker involved in the "complex attack"
The $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack is thought to be the largest of its kind in history - our cyber correspondent breaks down what we know

(Kitco Commentary) - The largest crypto theft in history hit while Bitcoin had already broken support, and the timing is right before the midterms.
Here’s how I am positioning before the election.
According to initial reports, about $6.3 billion was drained from the exchange’s hot wallets in minutes, and Bitcoin dropped to a six-week low.
That included 18,270 Bitcoin worth about $1.47 billion, more than 200,000 ETH, and billions in stablecoins.
Binance’s SAFU fund (Secure Asset Fund for Users) was set up in 2018 with $1 billion, and this hack is more than six times that size.
Binance says it will cover the rest with company funds.
Alphabet closed down more than 12% Thursday, the Nasdaq fell 1.4%, and Amazon and Intel both dropped hard after hours.
Ethereum fell to a two-month low around $2,178, and over $1.5 billion in leveraged positions got liquidated, most of them longs.

extraction.body: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record. The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets had been frozen but that many remained in the hands of the hackers, adding that it will "cover all losses". The company said while initial checks suggested an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, "our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach". Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor. Cyber-security firm Check Point said the unit is also known in the industry as Lazarus Group, which has been blamed for the 2025 hack. Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record". AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack. The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen. The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added. Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide. The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under its custody. The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world. Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack. For the last few years North Korea-linked operatives have focussed on attacking cryptocurrency companies for large thefts of digital tokens. Western security agencies have previously said stolen funds are used to finance North Korea's nuclear weapons and missile development programs. The regime has denied any involvement in hacks in the past. Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' Head of Research, urged every exchange to remain vigilant as the platforms are attractive targets for hackers due to the sheer value of assets. Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice." The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue. Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop. "That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions," he said in a statement. In an update, the company said in a statement on X that another investigation found there had been other breach points: "We are still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them." Check Point's Dave said this attack also resembled a hack on crypto exchange platform Bitget in September in which $388m (£289m) was lost: "This implies that attackers no longer need the vault keys. They target the systems and people with authority to use them." In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets. "Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said. Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack. World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it has worked with its partners to freeze stolen funds. Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation. Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue. Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply. If the accusations are true, the record-making heist shows how powerful suspected North Korean hackers have become. The cyber-attack, which the company describes as complex, is believed to be the largest ever of its kind. Cyber correspondent Joe Tidy explains more about what is suspected to be the biggest hack in history. sources.title: Thieves make off with $6.3B from Binance: 'Biggest hack in history'
passages: "Binance will cover all losses." "It's the biggest hack in history," Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR told Reuters.

Cryptocurrency giant Binance said Thursday that a major security incident had an estimated total impact of approximately $6.3 billion, with $3 billion already frozen, as the exchange temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals and pledged to cover customer losses.
Binance founder and majority shareholder Changpeng Zhao suggested the incident appeared to be a cyberattack, although the company has not officially characterized it as a hack.
It does look like a hack on Binance," Zhao wrote on X.
"Binance has confirmed a security incident and our teams are working around the clock to resolve it," the spokesperson said.

While investigating the possible cause, Binance said a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer may have allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.
Binance co-founder Yi He also addressed the incident on X, saying the exchange had temporarily disabled withdrawals while its security teams worked to secure the platform.
Binance said it would cover losses through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company funds, while promising to publish an updated Proof of Reserves once the incident is resolved.

MICHAEL SAYLOR PREDICTS BITCOIN WILL BLOW PAST $100K AS HE DECLARES NEW BULL MARKET UNDERWAY Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in potentially affected funds and said it was coordinating with relevant parties, according to Reuters.

"This is likely the largest crypto hack on record, but the key distinction is that it does not currently appear to be a solvency event for Binance," Fundstrat head of digital assets Sean Farrell said.

Binance has suspended all withdrawals after the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange fell victim to what appears to be the biggest heist in history. The exchange put the “estimated total impact” of the hack at about $6.3 billion and said around $3 billion of affected assets, mainly stablecoins that act as cash for the crypto market, had been frozen. An “initial investigation” suggested hackers had been able to compromise an engineer’s laptop and withdraw funds from the platform, Binance said, adding on Friday morning that further investigation “has uncovered additional points of breach.” The company is working with law enforcement. Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs linked the hack with a North Korean unit known as TraderTraitor, saying that the sums involved would make it “the largest crypto theft on record.” Last year, North Korean hackers stole crypto worth $1.5 billion in an attack on exchange Bybit. Peter Ward, of the Sejong Institute in Seoul, said North Korea had considerable expertise and offered “near-total protection to its hackers.” “Things may get a lot worse going forward,” he said. Binance said on Friday that it had “already reserved over $6.34 billion of company funds to cover this incident,” with $5 billion of the funds “already held in the exact token assets that were impacted.” The company said it was actively buying more tokens in order to cover the remaining amount. “This step can take longer because some tokens may have low liquidity,” and settlement “also takes time,” it said. The hack is a major blow to Binance, which was co-founded in 2017 by Changpeng Zhao and holds about $140 billion of digital assets. In 2023, the company pleaded guilty to US criminal charges related to breach of anti-money laundering laws and paid a $4.3 billion fine. Zhao, known as CZ, pleaded guilty to criminal charges relating to inadequate money laundering controls. He stepped down as chief executive and was pardoned last year by US President Donald Trump. The crypto market is in the grip of a prolonged downturn after a sharp sell-off late last year wiped more than $1tn from the combined capitalization of about 18,000 digital tokens. Richard Teng, co-chief executive of Binance, told customers that their “money is safe, and we’re covering every loss” from a reserve fund as well as “company funds.” Binance’s reserve fund holds about $1 billion worth of bitcoin, according to a company update from mid-October. Zhao said this leaves roughly $2 billion that the company still needs to cover, adding that the company owns shares in Elon Musk’s SpaceX worth more than $1 billion. “Remaining gap is (still painful, but) manageable,” he said in a post on X. North Korean hackers stole about $2 billion in cryptocurrency in 2025, a 50 percent increase from the year before, according to data from Chainalysis. Jeremy Allaire, head of Circle, the second-biggest stablecoin issuer, said $800 million of its USDC coin had been frozen amid “reports of a potential exploit” at Binance. Crypto companies can freeze the wallets in which stolen funds are moved or held. Analytics firm Elliptic said it had verified $2.8 billion of frozen crypto—mostly USDT and USDC—but that the hackers had moved the remainder into assets that could not be frozen, such as the ETH crypto token. “This is almost certainly the largest theft of any kind in history,” Elliptic said.

coreStoryFacts.text: North Korean hackers swiped $2 billion in 2025 , bringing the rogue regime's total haul since 2016 through the end of last year to $6.75 billion, according to data from crypto firm Chainalysis.

Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, was hit late Thursday by what investigators say is the biggest crypto hack in history , with $6.3 billion in funds impacted and roughly half of those assets frozen.

"This is likely the largest crypto hack on record, but the key distinction is that it does not currently appear to be a solvency event for Binance," Fundstrat head of digital assets Sean Farrell said.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Other major crypto assets also tumbled after the hack, with ether ( ETH-USD ) dropping 4% to around $2,200.
Binance's native token, BNB ( BND-USD ), also plunged by more than 6%.

The hackers appear to have compromised Binance's wallet-signing infrastructure, allowing them to authorize transactions that drained billions of dollars in cryptocurrency across multiple blockchains, according to the firms.
Binance, in its preliminary stage, has conducted an investigation into the hack, which suggests the incident may have begun with a compromised engineer's laptop.
The exchange added that it has found no evidence that wallet passwords were leaked.
Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter at Yahoo Finance.
Binance co-CEO Yi He said in a separate social media post Friday morning that customer withdrawals should resume within 48 hours.
Binance said it has money set aside in a Secure Asset Fund for Users to handle extreme cases, such as security breaches.

The exchange put the “estimated total impact” of the hack at about $6.3 billion and said around $3 billion of affected assets, mainly stablecoins that act as cash for the crypto market, had been frozen.
In 2023, the company pleaded guilty to US criminal charges related to breach of anti-money laundering laws and paid a $4.3 billion fine.

Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs linked the hack with a North Korean unit known as TraderTraitor, saying that the sums involved would make it “the largest crypto theft on record.” Last year, North Korean hackers stole crypto worth $1.5 billion in an attack on exchange Bybit.
Binance scrambles to freeze billions after record-breaking hack linked to North Korea.

Richard Teng, co-chief executive of Binance, told customers that their “money is safe, and we’re covering every loss” from a reserve fund as well as “company funds.” Binance’s reserve fund holds about $1 billion worth of bitcoin, according to a company update from mid-October.

An “initial investigation” suggested hackers had been able to compromise an engineer’s laptop and withdraw funds from the platform, Binance said, adding on Friday morning that further investigation “has uncovered additional points of breach.” The company is working with law enforcement.
Binance has suspended all withdrawals after the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange fell victim to what appears to be the biggest heist in history.
Crypto venues have become lucrative targets for hackers, with notable heists including $280 million stolen in April from the coffers of unregulated crypto exchange Drift.

Analytics firm Elliptic said it had verified $2.8 billion of frozen crypto—mostly USDT and USDC—but that the hackers had moved the remainder into assets that could not be frozen, such as the ETH crypto token.
Binance was ordered to wind down its EU operations in July after it failed to secure a license under the bloc’s new regulatory framework.
Binance works with Swiss banks Sygnum and Flow, the FT previously reported.

In the US, Binance operates under a separate entity from the rest of its global operations that is registered with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network and authorized to operate as a money transmitter in 32 states.

BOSTON/SINGAPORE/PARIS, Oct 30 (Reuters) - Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, worked on Friday to shore up public confidence after a record $6.3 billion hack of its platform, promising it would cover all losses from company funds and allow clients to trade again within days.

Cryptocurrency prices fell on news of the hack, which analysts blamed on North Korea and said could be the largest financial heist of all time. The publicly traded stocks of crypto-related firms Coinbase, Strategy and Robinhood slid.

Binance said customer funds were safe and it is working with industry partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion, but Binance co-CEO Yi He said in a post on X that $3 billion represented only about 2% of the company's total user assets and public reserves.

The exchange also said on Friday afternoon US eastern time that its technical team was targeting a resumption of withdrawal services within approximately 34 hours. Binance said it is conducting a full security review and plans an initial proof-of-reserves snapshot in 12 hours, with the results expected to be available by Monday.

Binance said it has set aside around $6.34 billion of company funds internally to cover the losses. The company has a $1 billion bitcoin reserve fund designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website. Binance founder Changpeng Zhao said on X that the company owned SpaceX shares worth more than $1 billion.

Binance's other co-CEO, Richard Teng, said in a post on X that the breach was a "complex attack" that was not carried out by one person and included a compromised laptop as well as malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity as it went along, "making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate."

The hackers were able to manipulate a system used to approve transactions to move money out of a Binance-controlled, internet-connected so-called "hot" wallet in a way that did not pass through normal approval controls, Teng said.
"Rest assured that we are working nonstop to resolve this, to make the users whole, and live up to your trust," Teng wrote.
The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs.
"This incident is almost certainly the single-largest-known theft of any kind," British blockchain analysts Elliptic said.

The bulk of the Binance heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis.
TRM said the attackers were able to order Binance wallets to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the FBI attributed to North Korea.
North Korea has âfor years â used state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue, according to US and South Korean authorities as well â as cybersecurity âexperts.
North Korea denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not respond to requests for comment.
US President Donald Trump, asked on Friday whether North Korean hackers were behind the theft, said he did not know but his administration is looking into it.

"It was a hack. That's the problem. You know the old-fashioned way when you used to sign a check, take it out. These are different. People never see the money anymore. So I've always felt it was a little bit dangerous," Trump told reporters at the White House when asked if he thought any of the stolen funds could be retrieved. "But no, they (Binance) say they have it pretty much under control."
Binance is working with the FBI and the US Secret Service, according to a person familiar with the situation.

The FBI said it is "aware of the incident and is engaged with relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity, evaluate potential impacts, and coordinate appropriate investigative steps."

The Secret Service said that its investigators "are working around the clock with our private-sector partners, including Circle, to identify, freeze, trace and recover funds stolen from Binance on Thursday."
Stablecoin issuer Tether said it froze nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million.

Abu Dhabi's Financial Services Regulatory Authority, which issued Binance's main operating license, said it is "engaging closely with Binance and monitoring the incident." Abu Dhabi-backed investment group MGX declined to comment. It became a minority investor in Binance last year.

Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for the crypto sector, which already was under pressure due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.
"It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralized exchanges," said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group.
Investor Michael Saylor, among bitcoin's most prominent supporters, said in a post on X that he expects Binance to "deliver" on ensuring no customers suffered losses.
"Our industry will learn from this incident, strengthen security and emerge stronger and more resilient," Saylor wrote on Friday.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report.
The heist at Binance drew a relatively measured response from crypto enthusiasts online.

On social media platform Reddit, discussions about the breach featured a mix of humor, confidence in the exchange's financial resources and questions about how such an enormous theft could have occurred.
The reaction stood in contrast to the panic surrounding the collapse of FTX in November 2022, when mounting doubts about the exchange's ability to repay customer funds triggered outrage online.

"Looking at all past data, we find that hot wallet hacks — even large ones — have historically not had a meaningful impact on future crypto returns," said Matt Hougan, chief investment officer at Bitwise Asset Management. "Investors tend to treat them as 'one-off events.'"

extraction.body: A record-breaking hack at Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, is a reminder of the risks investors take when trusting a company to hold their digital tokens. Binance said Friday that the security breach affected about $6.3 billion in client assets , making it the largest crypto hack on record. Around $3 billion of the affected assets has been frozen on blockchain networks, and the exchange says it has begun recovering some of them. Binance's initial investigation suggests hackers gained access to the firm's withdrawal systems and were able to make unauthorized transfers from the exchange's crypto wallets, according to the company . The company says it has found no evidence that the private keys controlling those wallets were leaked and is still investigating the full scope of the breach. The company says it will cover customers' losses . Binance maintains a roughly $1 billion emergency fund known as SAFU, which was created to protect customers in the event of a security breach. The company initially said SAFU and company funds would cover the losses, and has since said it has set aside more than $6.3 billion of its own funds. For crypto investors, the Binance breach highlights one of the risks of keeping assets on an exchange. While exchanges make it easier to buy, sell and store crypto, what happens after a hack can vary widely, including whether customers get their money back. Crypto exchange hacks aren't uncommon. Hackers stole roughly $1.5 billion from Dubai-based exchange Bybit in 2025, while Seychelles-registered Bitget lost more than $387 million in a hack in September 2026. But a hack doesn't necessarily mean customers will lose their money permanently. Stolen assets can sometimes be recovered or frozen — preventing the hackers from moving or cashing them out — and exchanges may also have insurance, dedicated emergency funds or other company resources available to cover losses. In Binance's case, roughly half of the affected assets have already been frozen, preventing some of the stolen crypto from being moved. Its roughly $1 billion SAFU emergency reserve provides another backstop, if needed. Customers don't always recover stolen digital assets quickly. New Zealand exchange Cryptopia was forced into liquidation months after a 2019 hack in which about NZ$30 million in crypto was stolen. The liquidation process stretched on for years, with the first distributions finally beginning in 2024 . "When you leave crypto on an exchange, you are relying on that company's controls and its balance sheet," says Martin Mulyadi, YHB Endowed Chair in Accounting and professor of accounting at Shenandoah University. "A pledge to make customers whole is only as strong as the resources behind it." When considering where to transact in and hold crypto, start by researching the exchange itself. The Securities and Exchange Commission recommends searching for customer complaints and checking how the exchange is regulated. U.S. customers can also check whether an exchange is registered with the Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, or FinCEN, using its online database . Registration can help confirm that you're dealing with an identifiable business operating within the U.S. regulatory system, though FinCEN cautions that registration isn't an endorsement of the company. Look for language explaining who owns your crypto and what the exchange can do with it. Phrases such as "you retain title" or assets being "held for your benefit" are good signs, Mulyadi says. Check whether customer assets are kept separate from the exchange's own, which can offer extra protection if the company fails. And find out whether the exchange can lend or otherwise use your crypto, which can expose your assets to additional risk. In the user agreement, check the exchange's limitation-of-liability section, Mulyadi says, and look at what insurance coverage the exchange offers and what it actually covers. "If a refund after a hack is at the exchange's discretion, it's a goodwill gesture, not a promise," Mulyadi says. Even strong language in the terms isn't a guarantee that your assets will be safe. FTX, the popular crypto exchange that collapsed in 2022, misappropriated billions of dollars in customer funds even though its terms said those assets belonged to customers, Mulyadi says. If you don't want to hold your crypto through an exchange, there's another option known as "self-custody." With self-custody, you use your own crypto wallet and control the private keys used to authorize transactions on the blockchain. Wallets typically come with a recovery phrase — essentially a master password that can be used to restore access to the wallet if you lose it. That gives you control of your crypto without relying on an exchange, but it also makes you responsible for keeping that information safe. And for anyone who's ever lost or forgotten a password, the risks of self-custody are real. With self-custody, there is "no help desk if you lose your recovery phrase," Mulyadi says. For many investors, Mulyadi says a middle ground is keeping only what they actively trade on an exchange and holding longer-term assets themselves, as long as they understand how to safely store and recover them. "Coins on an exchange are a promise from a company; coins in your own wallet are a responsibility you can't hand off," Mulyadi says. The company initially said SAFU and company funds would cover the losses, and has since said it has set aside more than $6.3 billion of its own funds.

For crypto investors, the Binance breach highlights one of the risks of keeping assets on an exchange. While exchanges make it easier to buy, sell and store crypto, what happens after a hack can vary widely, including whether customers get their money back.

Crypto exchange hacks aren't uncommon. Hackers stole roughly $1.5 billion from Dubai-based exchange Bybit in 2025, while Seychelles-registered Bitget lost more than $387 million in a hack in September 2026.

But a hack doesn't necessarily mean customers will lose their money permanently. Stolen assets can sometimes be recovered or frozen — preventing the hackers from moving or cashing them out — and exchanges may also have insurance, dedicated emergency funds or other company resources available to cover losses.

In Binance's case, roughly half of the affected assets have already been frozen, preventing some of the stolen crypto from being moved. Its roughly $1 billion SAFU emergency reserve provides another backstop, if needed.

Customers don't always recover stolen digital assets quickly. New Zealand exchange Cryptopia was forced into liquidation months after a 2019 hack in which about NZ$30 million in crypto was stolen. The liquidation process stretched on for years, with the first distributions finally beginning in 2024 .

"When you leave crypto on an exchange, you are relying on that company's controls and its balance sheet," says Martin Mulyadi, YHB Endowed Chair in Accounting and professor of accounting at Shenandoah University. "A pledge to make customers whole is only as strong as the resources behind it."

When considering where to transact in and hold crypto, start by researching the exchange itself. The Securities and Exchange Commission recommends searching for customer complaints and checking how the exchange is regulated.

U.S. customers can also check whether an exchange is registered with the Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, or FinCEN, using its online database . Registration can help confirm that you're dealing with an identifiable business operating within the U.S. regulatory system, though FinCEN cautions that registration isn't an endorsement of the company.

Look for language explaining who owns your crypto and what the exchange can do with it. Phrases such as "you retain title" or assets being "held for your benefit" are good signs, Mulyadi says. Check whether customer assets are kept separate from the exchange's own, which can offer extra protection if the company fails. And find out whether the exchange can lend or otherwise use your crypto, which can expose your assets to additional risk.
In the user agreement, check the exchange's limitation-of-liability section, Mulyadi says, and look at what insurance coverage the exchange offers and what it actually covers.
"If a refund after a hack is at the exchange's discretion, it's a goodwill gesture, not a promise," Mulyadi says.

Even strong language in the terms isn't a guarantee that your assets will be safe. FTX, the popular crypto exchange that collapsed in 2022, misappropriated billions of dollars in customer funds even though its terms said those assets belonged to customers, Mulyadi says.
If you don't want to hold your crypto through an exchange, there's another option known as "self-custody."

With self-custody, you use your own crypto wallet and control the private keys used to authorize transactions on the blockchain. Wallets typically come with a recovery phrase — essentially a master password that can be used to restore access to the wallet if you lose it.
That gives you control of your crypto without relying on an exchange, but it also makes you responsible for keeping that information safe.
And for anyone who's ever lost or forgotten a password, the risks of self-custody are real. With self-custody, there is "no help desk if you lose your recovery phrase," Mulyadi says.

For many investors, Mulyadi says a middle ground is keeping only what they actively trade on an exchange and holding longer-term assets themselves, as long as they understand how to safely store and recover them.
"Coins on an exchange are a promise from a company; coins in your own wallet are a responsibility you can't hand off," Mulyadi says.

sources.title: Binance targeted in $6.3 billion crypto heist, the largest ever
passages: The digital currency exchange Binance says it was the target of a $6.3 billion crypto heist Thursday, believed to be the largest ever recorded.
The previous record for a crypto heist was $1.5 billion that hackers from North Korea stole from Bybit in February 2025.
Binance is the world’s largest cryptocurrency trading platform by volume, with hundreds of thousands of users who buy, sell and store billions of dollars’ worth of digital currencies on the exchange.

The hack originated from a compromised laptop, it said, which allowed “an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.” “The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B,” Binance said late Thursday on X.
About $3 billion of crypto assets that transited through wallets connected to the hackers have so far been identified and frozen, the company said.

Binance’s founder, Changpeng Zhao, said, “As a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.” Zhao stepped down as the CEO of Binance in 2023 and pleaded guilty to breaking U.S. anti-money-laundering laws.

Unlike traditional bank deposits, funds kept in accounts with companies like Binance are not automatically insured against losses, potentially leaving any refunds up to the discretion of individual exchanges.
Binance cautioned that the full value of assets affected by the hack, as well as assets recovered or frozen, could change.

The massive breach of Binance occurs at a moment when cybersecurity defenses around the world are on high alert about the possibility of novel attacks facilitated by recent advances in artificial intelligence.
